content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any other documents relevant to gas properties, environmental policy, RPC geometry, and timing requirements. Assign numeric IDs 1–3 to the three candidate mixtures in the order listed in candidate_specs.md, and record each candidate’s GWP100 numerically with record_results."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard GWP100 <= 150 requirement using the recorded/documented values. For only the compliant candidate mixtures, run simulate_time_resolution at gas gaps 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0 mm. Record each simulated time resolution numerically, keyed by candidate ID and gap."},{"id":"s3","description":"From the coarse scan, identify the compliant candidate/gap region with the lowest time resolution. For each compliant candidate that is competitive or has the current best value, run a finer gap scan around its best coarse gap within 1–3 mm, using a spacing of about 0.25 mm or finer if needed. Record all time-resolution results."},{"id":"s4","description":"If the best point from the fine scan lies in the interior of the allowed gap range, run additional simulations bracketing it with smaller gap steps, about 0.05–0.10 mm, to locate the minimum time resolution more precisely. If the best point is at 1.0 or 3.0 mm, confirm the boundary optimum by simulating nearby allowed gaps. Record all results."},{"id":"s5","description":"Select the compliant mixture ID and gas gap that give the lowest simulated time resolution, ensuring the selected gap is between 1 and 3 mm and the mixture GWP100 is <= 150. Record the recommended numeric mixture ID, recommended gap in mm, selected GWP100, and selected time resolution for the reporting module."}]}
